item.title: Cricket Australia sets up 'safe space' for players to share sandpapergate experiences
item.description: Cricket Australia hopes the 'forum' will help the sport move on [Getty Images] Cricket Australia has launched an independent "forum" for cricketers and staff involved in the sandpapergate cheating scandal to share their version of events. In a memoir released earlier this month, former player Usman Khawaja claimed the entire Australia team knew about the plot to tamper with the ball in the final Test of their 2018 series with South Africa. His comments have led to a bitter split among former and current players, and have overshadowed the beginning of Australia's international cricket season. Chief executive Todd Greenberg said the forum was not a new investigation and no new penalties would be handed out. Nobody would be forced to take part, he added. However, he said he hoped the discussions would allow the sport to "move on". "The game is genuinely hurting at the moment. It's not good for anyone," he said. "We need to find a path through and we need some time to heal." The sandpapergate scandal is often described as one of Australian cricket's darkest days and was a source of national shame. Australian cricket's sandpapergate is back - and it cuts deep in a 'nation of good sports' Whole Australia team knew of sandpaper use - Khawaja An expedited investigation at the time found three players knew about the plan: captain Steve Smith, vice-captain David Warner and fellow batter Cameron Bancroft. They all faced lengthy bans. However Khawaja, Warner and another player on the tour, Chadd Sayers, have all now said they believed everyone knew. Current Australia captain Pat Cummins has rejected claims he knew sandpaper was being taken onto the field as "nonsense", and expressed hurt that Khawaja - his friend - had called his reputation into question. The release of Khawaja's book has also renewed scrutiny of Cricket Australia's initial investigation. A handful of players - including the batter - have said they were not interviewed for it, and Warner has accused the governing body of a "cover-up". "Over the past week we've had several different and conflicting accounts of what transpired in Cape Town in 2018 and it's been an incredibly difficult and uncomfortable time for the game and for everyone who was involved," Greenberg said on Friday. "What's become clear is that some players were not heard at that time. That opportunity now exists in a place without judgement, without sanction." He said the forum would be confidential – and that the Cricket Australia board would decide what information to make public. The incident had "a lot to do with the culture that existed back at the time", Greenberg said: a win-at-all-costs mentality which he admitted the governing body played a role in creating. He added that it is important the current Australian team be "afforded the space to perform at their best at what is a very important time and period for the game". item.title: MSU volleyball caps regular season with 4-set win over Michigan
item.description: EAST LANSING — The Michigan State volleyball team ended its regular season as well as it could have hoped. With a four-set win over rival Michigan on Senior Night. The Spartans improved to 18-9 overall, 8-9 in the Big Ten, with a 25-19, 25-18, 19-25, 25-15 win Tuesday, Nov. 17, inside the Breslin Center. The Spartans have now won 18 matches in back-to-back seasons for the first time since 2016-17. The Spartans hit .339 for the match and held the Wolverines (18-12, 7-10) to .244 hitting while leading in kills (55-47), service aces (11-1), digs (41-36) and total blocks (9-7). Making her return to the starting lineup after missing two matches with injury, senior outside hitter Alanna Bankston led MSU in kills with 17 while posting five digs and a service ace. Senior outside hitter Taylah Holdem tallied a season-high 15 kills on .387 hitting, while senior middle blocker Zora Hardison put up 12 kills on a .391 clip and added four total blocks. Redshirt sophomore setter Malayah Long provided 38 assists, three service aces and a team-high five total blocks with seven digs. Senior defensive specialist Ky Clayton led the Spartans with a career-high 11 digs and posted a team-best four service aces. Freshman libero Alana Whitfield recorded two service aces. MSU begins Big Ten tournament action on Friday, Nov. 20, at Fishers Event Center in Fishers, Indiana. — MSU Athletic Communications This article originally appeared on Lansing State Journal: MSU volleyball caps regular season with 4-set win over Michigan

item.title: Barcelona tried to sign Joško Gvardiol last summer – but the operation seems impossible now
item.description: MANCHESTER, ENGLAND - OCTOBER 31: Joko Gvardiol of Manchester City during the Premier League 2026/27 match between Manchester City and Brighton & Hove Albion at Etihad Stadium on October 31, 2026 in Manchester, United Kingdom. (Photo by Visionhaus/Getty Images) | Visionhaus/Getty Images Barcelona tried to sign Joško Gvardiol at the same time as they signed Rodri from Manchester City , according to a new report from Diario AS . Barça succeeded in signing Rodri, but they could not pry Gvardiol off City, because he has a contract until 2031. He was thought to be the ideal signing to bolster the defense: a young, experienced, and talented center-back who can operate as a full-back. Now, Barcelona sporting director Deco is said to be combing the market for a central defender, and the chances of signing Gvardiol in the winter transfer window are slim to none. Only a dramatic turn of events involving a punishment for City’s digressions over Premier League financial charges could turn the situation. Barcelona are thin at center-back and have not properly replaced Iñigo Martínez, who left last year in a transfer to Saudi Arabia. Pau Cubarsí and Gerard Martín are the sure starters, but only Andreas Christensen is a pure central defender among the substitutes, and he struggles with recurring injuries. Barcelona have some options in the position, but they are not ideal. Jules Koundé and Eric Garcia are thought of as full-backs, while Frenkie de Jong, a midfielder, has played in central defense on an emergency basis. Barça have been linked with several defenders, but they don’t have space in La Liga’s Financial Fair Play controls to make signings unless they let players go. Jonathan Tah has been mentioned as a potential target, but again, the report says he is probably too expensive for a winter signing. Natan (Real Betis) and Jon Martín (Real Sociedad) are seen as more realistic targets. Cristian Romero, then at Tottenham Hotspur, now at Atlético Madrid, was also considered in the past, though ultimately passed over as the club was looking for a left-footer. Alessandro Bastoni from Inter was another target, though Inter made sure to keep him, and Barça’s interest cooled off.

item.title: Ball State football falls to Ohio in road MACtion game | Final score, takeaways
item.description: Ball State nearly pulled off one of the most stunning victories of the Mid-American Conference football season, but the Cardinals fell just short on the road once again. Ball State (3-8, 2-5 MAC) lost its third-straight game, falling 35-28 at Ohio (8-3, 6-1 MAC) in its final midweek MACtion game of the season on Tuesday, Nov. 17. The Cardinals looked ready to spoil their opponents' season after a strong first half and held a six-point lead at halftime, but the Bobcats reclaimed the momentum with a pick-six in the second half and eventually held on for the win. Ball State is now 1-13 on the road under head coach Mike Uremovich, while Ohio's FBS-best home winning streak extends to 18 games. More: Our live updates from Ball State football at Ohio in midweek MACtion Here are three takeaways from Ball State football's MACtion loss to Ohio. Tale of two halves for Ball State offense Ball State followed up last week's dreadful outing with its best half of offensive football all season. The Cardinals scored points on four of their five drives in the first half and took a six-point lead into the locker room. Quarterback Keldric Luster was nearly flawless, going 11-for-20 passing for 208 yards and two touchdowns, including an 80-yard touchdown pass to receiver Eli Hohlt that was the Cardinals' longest passing play all season. Ball State also ran the ball effectively, racking up 118 total yards on the ground with six explosive runs of 10 or more yards. The second half was a different story. Ball State's first four drives after halftime went turnover, three-and-out, turnover, three-and-out. The second turnover gave the Bobcats the lead as Ohio safety Darren James-Hamilton took advantage of Luster's worst throw of the year, turning it into a 34-yard pick-six to put the Bobcats back in front. After the ensuing three-and-out, the Bobcats went up by eight with touchdown drive. Ball State's offense finally woke up in the fourth quarter with a 10-play, 68-yard touchdown drive to tie the game with just over two minutes remaining. The Bobcats reclaimed the lead quickly, though, and the Cardinals' game-winning drive was stopped. QB runs kill Ball State defense Ohio ran a lot of read options and speed options with mobile quarterbacks Nick Poulos and Levi Davis, who came in for an extended drive in the third quarter. Poulos ran eight times for 58 yards and two touchdowns, while Davis had several long runs on his snaps but only finished with 10 rushing yards after taking a long sack. The options also opened things up for running backs Duncan Brune and Victor Rosa, who combined for 118 rushing yards on 17 carries. The Cardinals' defense has had trouble with mobile quarterbacks all season. Liberty's DeShawn Purdie, Kent State's Dru DeShields and UMass' Pop Watson III have all given Ball State's defense trouble with both their arms and their legs this season. item.title: No. 15 Vanderbilt Basketball Continues Perfect Start With Another Blowout Win
item.description: Photo by: Steve Roberts Vanderbilt Dominates Eastern Illinois to Remain Undefeated Vanderbilt basketball continued its impressive start to the season Tuesday night, delivering a dominant 96-50 victory over Eastern Illinois at Memorial Gymnasium. The No. 15 Commodores controlled the matchup from the opening minutes, using an explosive offensive performance and strong defense to improve to 5-0. Coming into the contest, Vanderbilt had already established itself as one of the most exciting teams in the SEC. The Commodores entered with a perfect 4-0 record and an opportunity to continue building momentum before the schedule becomes more challenging. Eastern Illinois entered the matchup looking to pull off an upset, but Vanderbilt quickly showed why it was the favorite. Vanderbilt Takes Control Before Halftime The Commodores started the game with some early competition from the Panthers. Eastern Illinois managed to stay within striking distance during the opening portion of the first half, trailing 25-21 with just over seven minutes remaining. However, Vanderbilt quickly shifted the momentum. The Commodores closed the first half with a 12-2 scoring run, creating separation and taking a 43-26 advantage into the locker room. Tyler Tanner helped lead the offensive effort, giving Vanderbilt a consistent scoring presence. The Commodores also received contributions from Sebastian Williams-Adams and Ace Glass III, allowing the offense to remain productive from multiple positions. Eastern Illinois struggled to find consistent scoring opportunities as Vanderbilt’s defense began taking control of the game. Commodores Pull Away in the Second Half Any opportunity for an Eastern Illinois comeback quickly disappeared after halftime. Vanderbilt opened the second half with a 17-5 run, extending its advantage and putting the game out of reach. The Commodores were especially impressive shooting the basketball. Vanderbilt finished the night shooting 61.7 percent from the field and knocked down 12 three pointers. The offensive performance was led by Tanner, who finished with 21 points while shooting eight of 11 from the field. He also scored 14 points in the second half, helping Vanderbilt continue extending its lead. Williams-Adams delivered one of his best performances of the season, finishing with a career-high 16 points. Glass also contributed 16 points, giving the Commodores three players with at least 16 points. Vanderbilt’s defensive performance was just as impressive. The Commodores held Eastern Illinois to 32 percent shooting and forced 16 turnovers. Those mistakes created additional scoring opportunities, with Vanderbilt turning them into 23 points. The Commodores also dominated inside, outscoring the Panthers 46-16 in points in the paint. item.title: ESPN analyst sees worrying regression in Josh Allen despite NFL history
item.description: Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images ESPN analyst Mina Kimes believes Josh Allen has taken a step backwards this season despite leading the Buffalo Bills to an 8-1 start and continuing to make NFL history. Allen has been one of the league’s leading quarterbacks in 2026, helping Buffalo overcome injuries to key wide receivers and inconsistent performances elsewhere on offence. However, Kimes believes his performances have not matched the standard he set last season, despite his impressive numbers. Mina Kimes questions Josh Allen’s performances despite historic numbers Speaking on The Mina Kimes Show while discussing the leading NFL MVP candidates with Ben Solak, Kimes said: “Josh Allen, we haven’t spent much time talking about. Like I said, I think he’s asked to do a lot, but he’s obviously playing worse than he did last year, to my eyes, so I just don’t see it personally.” Allen’s statistics offer a different perspective. Through nine games, he has completed 65 per cent of his passes, down from 69.3 per cent last season, but remains on course to match his 25 passing touchdowns from 2025. He is also projected to finish with more passing yards, although his current interception rate puts him on course for 13, three more than last season. There has been a significant improvement in his ball security as a runner, too. Allen has yet to fumble this season after recording six fumbles in 2025. NFL analyst Michael F. Florio highlighted another potential milestone, writing: “Josh Allen is on pace for 25 pass TDs and 21 rush TDs. There’s never been a 20-20 season.” Allen has already made history this season. His two rushing touchdowns and one passing touchdown in Buffalo’s 31-12 win over the New York Jets took his career total to 325. That moved him past Peyton Manning’s record of 322 total touchdowns by a player in their first 10 NFL seasons. Allen has reached the mark in just nine seasons. The Bills quarterback now has 24 total touchdowns in 2026, more than 15 NFL teams. While Kimes has questioned his performances, Allen’s production and Buffalo’s strong start suggest he remains firmly in the MVP conversation. item.title: Cunningham, Jenkins lead surge as Pistons snap Spurs’ 12-game winning streak with 105-93 victory
item.description: Nov 17, 2026; San Antonio, Texas, USA; Detroit Pistons guard Cade Cunningham (2) during the first half against the San Antonio Spurs at Frost Bank Center. Mandatory Credit: Scott Wachter-Imagn Images Scott Wachter/IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect SAN ANTONIO — Cade Cunningham scored 27 points, Daniss Jenkins had 21 of his 25 in the second half and the Detroit Pistons snapped San Antonio’s 12-game winning streak, toppling the Spurs 105-93 on Tuesday night. Victor Wembanyama had 25 points and 18 rebounds for San Antonio, which had not lost since Oct. 23, when it fell to 0-2. Spurs guard Dylan Harper finished with 20 points but exited with 53 seconds remaining after his left foot slid out from under him and he tumbled to the court. His status is unknown. Ausur Thompson finished with 14 points, 12 assists, nine rebounds and five steals for Detroit, which overcame a sluggish start to win after getting swept by San Antonio last season. The Pistons outscored the Spurs 52-39 in the second and third quarters while shooting 51%. San Antonio lost for the first time when leading by double digits. Wembanyama had 10 points in the opening quarter, highlighted by throwing the ball off the backboard over an outstretched Thompson to assist on his own left-handed dunk. San Antonio had five dunks in the first quarter but it was Cunningham who provided the exclamation with a one-handed slam against a late-closing Wembanyama. Detroit went on a 21-7 run in the second quarter, closing with a 13-5 burst when Wembanyama sat, to tie the game at 47 after trailing by 14 in the period. The Spurs outscored the Pistons by 12 when Wembanyama was on the court in the first half and were minus-12 when he sat. Thompson and Cunningham combined for 21 points in the second quarter as Detroit outscored San Antonio 29-21 in taking its first lead at 55-54 into halftime. Detroit was without Jalen Duren (strained right hamstring), Duncan Robinson (strained left quadriceps) and Isaiah Joe (right hip contusion). Up next Pistons: At New Orleans on Wednesday. Spurs: Host Los Angeles Clippers on Thursday.

item.title: Ciryl Gane Favorably Compared to Muhammad Ali by Jon Jones
item.description: Ciryl Gane Jon Jones Muhammad Ali Getty UFC legend Jon Jones favorably compared UFC heavyweight champion Ciryl Gane to boxing great Muhammad Ali following UFC 334. Gane outstruck Josh Hokit in the UFC 334 main event to collect his first successful defense of the UFC heavyweight title. In the fight, Gane landed 237 significant strikes, including 170 head strikes. With Gane showing such impressive boxing, it led to Jones, his former rivals, comparing him to the great Ali. Jon Jones Compares Ciryl Gane to Muhammad Ali Taking to his social media, Jones said that Gane reminds him of Ali in that he has terrific footwork and an elite jab in MMA. “Ciryl Gane show glimpses of Muhammad Ali. So light on his feet just popping that jab. Float like a butterfly sting like a bee,” Jones wrote on his X . Ciryl Gane show glimpses of Muhammad Ali. So light on his feet just popping that jab. Float like a butterfly sting like a bee. https://t.co/ZHv4ICjo4S — Jonny Meat (@JonnyBones) November 17, 2026 Would Jon Jones Fight Ciryl Gane Again? Jones and Gane have fought before, with Jone submitting Gane in the first round with a guillotine choke when the two met at UFC 285 in March 2023. But since that fight, Jones has barely fought, while Gane has collected ton more MMA experience, so it would be really interesting to see if these two ever fought again how a rematch would go. Would Gane be the guy who could coax Jones out of retirement to come back and fight again? Probably not, as Jones already has a win over him and would likely prefer to fight someone else and take on a new challenge if he ever did fight again. But there is no doubt that it would be a very interesting rematch if these two rivals ever did fight again, knowing how much Gane has improved since the first time these two fighters met nearly four years ago. In the meantime, Gane will prepare for his next challenger, who will likely be a rematch with Alex Pereira if the Brazilian gets past Sergei Pavlovich at UFC 335 next month. Should Pereira lose that fight, however, it wouldn’t be a surprise to see Alexander Volkov get the title shot instead, which would actually be a trilogy bout against Gane, who has beaten Volkov two times already. The penultimate week of the college football regular season is here, as teams continue to jockey for playoff positioning and bowl berths. item.title: Fort Defiance volleyball chases elusive state title
item.description: Fort Defiance is hoping a third trip to the state championship match will be the magical one. Fort swept Madison County 25-14, 25-18, 25-13 in the Class 2 state semifinals Nov. 17, earning another trip to the title game in Salem Saturday, Nov. 21. Fort will play John Battle, a straight set winner over Ridgeview in the other semifinal match Tuesday night. Battle's last appearance in the state championship game was 1999 when the Trojans lost to Wilson Memorial. One connection between that year and this one is that Wilson was coached by the current principal at Fort Defiance, Fonda Morris. Fort has made the trip to Salem the past two seasons only to come up short both years. They get a chance to redeem those defeats at noon Saturday. "I just can't count my blessings enough," said senior Norah Anderson of going to her third state championship game. "Every time I just look back on my volleyball career and what I've experienced at Fort, it's so special. Not everybody gets to experience this. I'm overwhelmed with joy and just gratefulness." Anderson is one of four seniors on the team who will be trying to end their high school volleyball careers in style. "It means the world," said senior Madison Bragg. "It's amazing." On Tuesday though it was a pair of juniors who did most of the damage offensively. Harper Carter had 14 digs and Caroline Hanger had 11. Carter didn't have an error on the night and finished with a .700 hitting percentage for the match. "I was seeing the block very well," said Carter, in her first year on Fort's varsity team. "My coaches, before the game, they were like swing, just swing really hard. Do whatever you want and they won't be able to pick it up." The coaches were right. Madison had absolutely no answer for the 6-foot middle blocker. Fort coach Amber Pitsenbarger told Carter after the match that she was a beast. "She was awesome," Pitsenbarger said. "She's that player who is going to take it in her hands and make sure that she really puts the ball down. She did a great job with that." Sophomore Abbi Bright had 14 digs to lead Fort defensively while Hanger added 12 digs and freshman Maddie Gale and Anderson both had nine. Gale and Anderson also both had three aces to lead the team. Fort had beaten Madison a week earlier in the regional championship. Not much changed this time around, although the Mountaineers put up a fight in the first two sets. In the opening set there were three lead changes and four ties but, with Fort in front 13-11, senior Livia Clinedinst got a kill to start an 8-0 run by Fort, who cruised to the win after that. Madison led 4-1 in the second set before a pair of Hanger kills started a 5-0 run to give Fort the lead for good. Madison hung around, trailing 19-17, before Fort got two straight Carter kills to score the next five points. "We didn't play the strongest there at the beginning," said Pitsenbarger. item.title: LeBron James claims copying Michael Jordan created ‘bad habits’ in his game that still affect him
item.description: Photo by Kevin Mazur/Getty Images LeBron James has made it no secret that he grew up idolising Michael Jordan, but this idolisation may have led James to develop a huge weakness. James was inspired by Jordan in his younger days to pursue basketball, even making the Bulls star’s iconic #23 jersey his own But after having time to reflect, wanting to be like Mike may have led James to emulate his idol in ways that just didn’t suit him. LeBron James admits trying to ’emulate’ Michael Jordan’s shooting has affected his career Speaking on his Mind the Game podcast with Steve Nash, LeBron James gave insight into how he developed his shot by watching Michael Jordan’s iconic fadeaway shot. James admitted he tried to emulate his shot, but he didn’t account for Jordan’s balance while shooting, which led to him adopting some bad habits in his technique that still affect him to this day. LeBron James: “My shooting journey is like literally watching Michael Jordan. But the thing I didn’t realise is how balanced Michael Jordan… I saw a fadeaway. So when I started to see that I had some athletic genes, I maybe picked up some bad habits in my shooting. Because I can emulate that. So I was shooting fadeaways as like a freshman in high school, and I would make them. “But I didn’t realise that I was picking up bad habits along that time because I didn’t study the fact that, okay, yeah, MJ’s doing that, but you’re not even seeing how on balance he is. You have no idea that, or he’s been doing this for years and years and years, and you’re just trying to pick it up because you’re trying to emulate him.” Steve Nash: “And were you fading unnecessarily? You’re like open, but you’re still kind of fading to be like MJ.” LeBron James: “And almost like still to this day, some of it is still in my shot, of like leaning back. I still, right off the top. And I think it had a lot to do with MJ.” While some might read these comments from James as a jab at his idol, the four-time NBA champion is actually praising the meticulous nature of Jordan’s shooting. He admitted that he didn’t fully grasp everything that goes into being able to shoot like Jordan, especially for him as a taller and bulkier player. When he first entered the NBA, James’ jump shot was one of his biggest weaknesses. But over the years, as the NBA moved into a more shooting-oriented style of play, LeBron developed his game further, and now has some reliable jump shots that he can make with relative ease. item.description: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - NOVEMBER 08: Head Coach Nick Sirianni of the Philadelphia Eagles walks on the field prior to the game against the New York Giants at Lincoln Financial Field on November 08, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Todd Olszewski/Getty Images) Getty The Philadelphia Eagles‘ attention has at this point likely shifted towards the 2027 season, given that they currently stand at 2-7 at the bottom of the already bad NFC East. Although the team’s struggles are understandable given the injuries to Jalen Hurts, Devonta Smith and others, in addition to the team enacting a sneaky fire sale that saw the departures of center Cam Jurgens and defensive tackle Jordan Davis, many fans taken this opportunity to call for the Eagles to move off head coach Nick Sirianni in favor of someone new. Whilst recent reports have claimed that Sirianni’s job is safe for the moment, a spanner could be thrown into the works with a separate report concerning newly-minted NBC Sports analyst Mike Tomlin. According to uStadium, the former Super Bowl-winning coach who spent 19 years as the head coach of the Pittsburgh Steelers and never had a losing season, could be tempted by the Eagles head coaching job, as well as that of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. Asked someone in the know which potential head coaching openings might entice Mike Tomlin to return to coaching: His answer: Buccaneers and Eagles. — uSTADIUM (@uSTADIUM) November 17, 2026 Eagles Job Could ‘Entice’ Mike Tomlin, per Report “Asked someone in the know which potential head coaching openings might entice Mike Tomlin to return to coaching: His answer: Buccaneers and Eagles.” The account posted on X on Nov. 17. This report has not been verified by Tomlin himself, nor other top-tier league insiders such as Ian Rapoport or Adam Schefter. But if it is true, it would certainly throw a spanner in the works for the Eagles’ decision making on Sirianni’s future, which starts and ends with owner Jeffrey Lurie. Would the Eagles Hire a Defensive-Minded Head Coach? The one sticking point could be the fact that Tomlin is a defensive-minded head coach, having previously spent time as the defensive coordinator of the Minnesota Vikings in 2006 before being swooped up by the Steelers. Lurie has not hired a defensive-minded coach since adding Ray Rhodes back in 1995; his first head coaching appointment after purchasing the team in 1994. And that trend does not feel accidental. But for a coach of Tomlin’s class, caliber and experience; and one who is still just 54 years of age, the Eagles owner could be willing to break his own informal rule if Tomlin is willing to return to coaching after a year out. The Longhorns (8-2, 5-2 SEC) are the No. 5 team in the CFP rankings, one spot above its No. 6 spot last week and two spots above its No. 7 ranking in the first CFP rankings released Nov. 3. Texas leads the nation with five wins over top-25 teams. Alabama is tied with nine other programs for second-most with three wins over then-top 25 teams, and the Crimson Tide have only lost to No. 1 Georgia and at No. 8 Tennessee. An expanded College Football Playoff keeps two-loss teams alive and well given a difficult schedule. A three-loss team could even qualify in the right circumstance (get ready for four, and even five-loss teams in the 24-team playoff , by the way).
